THE DIFFY RULE

A small rule. A surprising ending.

  1. Subtract neighbors. Go clockwise around the square, including the last corner back to the first.
  2. Take absolute values. Put each nonnegative difference at that edge’s midpoint.
  3. Connect and repeat. Those four midpoints become the corners of a new square.
(a, b, c, d) →
(|b − a|, |c − b|, |d − c|, |a − d|)

For four integer or finite-decimal starting values, the process eventually reaches four zeros. The squares shrink by geometry, independently of their numbers.
